subject: Four more unreachable-trigger defects incl. the cost telemetry; FINGERPRINT tasks 2-5 built, lookahead assertion passing, holdout fixed
body:
Four more instances of the defect I found last tick, and the first four tasks of your
build order are done.

THE SWEEP. Last tick I found a report that could only fire on a day rollover, which our runs never
reach. I asked which others share that trigger. The daily summary calls exactly three reports -
EXIT-COND, TYPE-I/II and FULL-PATH/RESIDUAL - and all three appear zero times across all six
retained logs, along with the daily summary itself. An earlier warrant had already seen those zeroes
and blamed the output routing, and fixed the routing. That fix was correct and insufficient: routing
was never the binding constraint, because the call itself never happens. Correctly routed output of
a function that is never invoked is still nothing. All three now also fire at shutdown.

THE FOURTH ONE IS DIFFERENT AND MATTERS MORE. The execution-cost summary - spread, slippage, reject
rate, average cost per trade - is still going to the terminal tab and never the permanent record;
the earlier routing fix missed it. Unlike the other three it does fire, so that data has been
produced and discarded every single run. It matters because our own edge measurement put realistic
costs at 19 to 41 times the best gross expectancy found. A cost series that never reaches the record
cannot be read back when the edge decision is finally made. Now routed.

I checked whether any criterion was passing on evidence that never existed. None was - C6.2 is met
on a file the calibration path writes, and the other two are unautomated. The defect cost evidence,
not board correctness.

YOUR TASKS 2 THROUGH 5 ARE BUILT. The fingerprint now records what was true at every one of 111,548
bars - including the declined ones, which is your RULE 2.3 and the row you say nobody records. Six
indicators named before any looking and grouped by speed, because without that grouping "which side
is early" cannot be computed at all. Every reading stored as a percentile of its own last 200, which
is what will let a finding be tested on a second market. Your three disagreement fields replace the
hundred and twenty pairwise ones.

The part I am most confident in: your RULE 1.3 says assert no-lookahead in code, not in intention.
So the module recomputes sampled rows from a history truncated at that bar and requires every field
to come back identical - anything peeking forward changes when the future is removed. It passed.
That guard is what makes everything downstream worth anything.

And the holdout is fixed and written down before any testing: the latest 20% by time on all four
datasets, with dataset hashes and touched=false. The latest slice rather than a random interior
block, because a random block can be reached by interpolation from both sides, and the real question
is whether a finding survives forward. The splitter refuses to run without a recorded boundary - a
holdout you can recompute after seeing a result is not a holdout.

Board unchanged at 17 met, 7 not met. Seven compiles today, all clean.

Next is your staged test - Stage 1, ten families pooled. It needs a per-bar outcome first, which I
will build from your section 7 baseline stop. Still nothing needed from you except the MT4
permission, which gates task 1's answer and C1.1.
